This explains why g and r have brightened far faster and higher than the Type Ia templates forecast in the last few days.
proposals.name: Unseen microlens amplification
proposals.predicts: Flux will reach a sharp symmetric peak then fall as the mirror image of the rise with essentially constant g-r color, rather than the asymmetric, reddening decline of a Type Ia supernova.

proposals.idea: At galactic latitude 10 degrees an unseen foreground star is crossing the line of sight to a red background star, and its point-lens magnification is producing the smooth, accelerating rise seen in both bands. This is gravitational magnification of an existing star rather than a new explosion, so the red colour is the source's intrinsic colour.
proposals.name: Milky Way microlensing event
proposals.predicts: It predicts strictly achromatic evolution with constant g-r colour, a symmetric peak soon after now, and a fall that mirrors the rise back to the pre-event baseline, unlike a supernova's asymmetric, colour-evolving decline.

proposals.idea: A steady underlying star or host was imperfectly removed by the reference template, leaving a constant subtraction residual at this position. A slow epoch-dependent zero-point drift then scales that residual upward in both bands, mimicking a rapidly brightening transient brighter than the fitted supernovae.
proposals.name: Drifting calibration subtraction residual
proposals.predicts: It predicts a continued near-linear rise in flux with independent g and r drift rates and no imminent supernova-like peak, turnover, decline, or cooling colour evolution.
